chunks: And the one who narrated it: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from al-Halabi from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked about a man who leaves his house intending to travel while he is fasting, so he said:
"If he leaves before midday, let him break his fast and make up that day; and if he leaves after midday, let him complete his day."

key_terms.وَلْيَقْضِ: and let him make up (the fast)
key_terms.يَنْتَصِفَ النَّهَارُ: midday / when half the day has passed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a fast if a person starts traveling before or after midday?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the critical criterion of 'midday' (zawal) as the dividing line for travel-related fasting exemptions, a ruling foundational to Shia jurisprudence. It clarifies that breaking the fast is mandatory if departure occurs before noon, whereas departing after noon validates the day's fast, reflecting the principle of ease in travel. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on precise temporal markers in determining the validity of religious obligations during journeys.
